extracted.intended_audience: Mathematics Stack Exchange users (question askers and community reviewers/moderators)
extracted.subtask_description: Explanation of what it means for a question to be closed on Mathematics Stack Exchange, the categories/reasons for closure, how closure/reopening works, and who may cast close/reopen votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of closure
rubrics_metrics.description: Closed questions cannot be answered, but can be edited to make them eligible for reopening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your question is closed, you will receive private feedback on the reason why it was closed. Editing a closed question to address the close reason can make it eligible for reopening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate
rubrics_metrics.description: This question has been asked before and already has an answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fundamental goal of closing duplicate questions is to help people find the right answer by getting all of those answers in one place. See the help center article about duplicate questions for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-specific reason (previously Off-topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: This question doesn’t meet a Mathematics Stack Exchange guideline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each community decides which specific topics are and are not allowed on their site; view the list of disallowed subjects in the help center or consult this site's Meta for specific guidance. If you believe the question can be reworded to fit within the scope, consider editing the question or leaving comments for improvement. Note: choosing this close reason will present another set of options (which vary by site), and site moderators' custom close reasons may be shown first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not about math / out of scope
rubrics_metrics.description: This question does not appear to be about math, within the scope defined in the help center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it truly belongs to a different topic area, consider editing to bring it into scope or flag/move it as appropriate. Refer to site scope guidance in the help center or Meta.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belongs on another site (migration)
rubrics_metrics.description: This question belongs on another site in the Stack Exchange network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When this option is selected, the voter is shown a list of sites that the question can be migrated to (the site's Meta appears by default; staff-added migration paths may appear). Site moderators may migrate the post to any site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other — add a comment (custom close reason)
rubrics_metrics.description: A custom close reason can be specified when none of the existing reasons suffice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing this option opens a text box initially filled with: "I’m voting to close this question because " prompting the voter to provide a specific custom reason. (This option is not shown in the flagging dialog to users without the close/reopen votes privilege.) The custom reason will also be publicly displayed as a comment on the question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs details or clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: This question should include more details and clarify the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit your post to be more specific about what you're looking for, and be sure to address any concerns that other users brought up in the comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs more focus
rubrics_metrics.description: This question currently includes multiple questions in one. It should focus on one problem only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a question has many valid answers (but no way to determine which is correct), it needs to be narrowed. This can often be fixed by breaking the post into multiple questions or by focusing on a specific part of the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion-based
rubrics_metrics.description: This question is likely to be answered with opinions rather than facts and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such discussions don't fit the site's Q&A format. It's often possible to rewrite opinion-based questions to focus on a more fact-based line of questioning; if you see a way to do this, consider editing the question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging vs close vote behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Users with the 'flag posts' privilege see largely the same list when attempting to flag a question and select 'needs improvement'; users with close/reopen votes privilege will cast a close vote instead of a flag when using these reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes how the UI/privileges interact: attempting to flag using a close reason will cast a close vote rather than a flag if the user has the close/reopen privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close/reopen privileges and mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Users with 3000 reputation can cast up to 50 close votes per day. When a question reaches 5 close votes, it is marked as Closed and will no longer accept answers. Users with the same privilege may also vote to reopen questions; each user may only vote to close and reopen a given question once. Moderators may close or reopen any question with a single vote, without the usual restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implications: close votes are community-moderation actions limited by per-user/day caps and a 5-vote threshold for ordinary users; diamond moderators override these limits. A user's prior close/reopen vote on a question prevents repeating the same action after a reopen cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopen process and reopen queue triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Any closed question that receives one reopen vote by a user with sufficient reputation is automatically added to a reopen queue for community review. Any question with significant edits that address the close reason(s) gets added to the reopen queue. If enough community members agree, the question will be reopened and can accept answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edits addressing the close reason are a primary path to reopening. Community review in the reopen queue determines whether the question should be reopened; sufficient community agreement is required.
